### Exercise 1

`geno_data` (`genotypes.csv`) contains some genotyping array data.

- Check that you can understand what the variables (probably) mean

- What is n? What is p?

- Make some plots. What can you learn?

- What kind of structure do you think *could* exist in this dataset?

- Do any of the plots you made demonstrate that structure?

```{webr}
library("tidyverse")
# Read data
geno_data <- read.csv("https://jmc108.github.io/hugen2073-textbook/exercises/11_machine_learning/genotypes.csv")
# Peek at variables
geno_data[1:10,1:6]
# n and p
dim(geno_data)
# Scatterplot of 2 variables
geno_data %>% 
  ggplot()+
  geom_point(aes(x=rs1695824, y=rs13328662))
# Add some noise to clarify
geno_data %>% 
  ggplot()+
  geom_jitter(aes(x=rs1695824, y=rs13328662), width=0.05, height=0.05)
```

:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}

### Exercise 2

Try the same thing for another dataset, `X` (contained in `pcadata.Rdata`).

```{webr}
# Load data
load(url("https://jmc108.github.io/hugen2073-textbook/exercises/11_machine_learning/pcadata.RData"))
# Inspect
X[1:5,1:5]
dim(X)
# Scatterplot of two features
plot(X[,1],X[,300])
```


:::
